panel.rule: total>=40 OR bug>=5 OR safety>=5 OR urgency>=5

scores.note: Adds hv_mps table entry (init 0xFF, ~sum&0x7F|0x40) in ChecksumConverter.cc only. Purely additive, opt-in, useful only if a Spellman MPS supply is on the network. Runtime: IOC with out '%s%<hv_mps>' for '123456789' sent suffix 'c' = 0x63, matching the table comment. Applies clean on pin and on pin+local patches, builds with 0 warnings.

Replaces streamApp/asynRegistrars.dbd (deleted) by asyn.dbd/drvAsynIPPort/drvAsynSerialPort includes with vxi11 commented out. Same goal as local StreamDevice-no-vxi11.p0.patch, which edits the file F2 deletes: on baseline the patch hunk is rejected ('1 out of 1 hunk ignored'). Only affects the demo streamApp, not libstream. Drops asynRecord.dbd and the IPServerPort registrar. Applies and builds on bare pin (chain A) and testChecksum passes, but zero marginal value over the local patch; adopting it means retiring that patch.
One-word typo in a debug() format string in StreamCore.cc. No behavior change. Applies clean, builds.

Input checksums are now computed on the unmodified input when a regsub precedes them. Adds needs_original_format enum value and a delta-tracking branch in StreamCore::matchInput; ChecksumConverter::parse now returns it for EVERY input checksum, so all input checksums take the new path. Real bug but only reachable with the regsub converter, which needs PCRE; the environment builds with PCRE= empty. Runtime evidence: with the upstream added test line, IOC prints 'No converter registered for format %/' and the whole protocol fails to compile, so the new upstream test cannot run in this environment. With the regsub lines removed, testChecksum (all checksums) passes on pin+F4, F4+F5, and the full chain. Defect: StreamFormatTypeStr[] was not extended.

Warning cleanup: PRINTF_SIZE_T_PREFIX macro in debug formats and a size_t loop var in the Windows-only win_console_init; _MINGW guard. Hunks patch code added by F4, so it fails alone on the pin and on the baseline ('Hunk #1 FAILED at 1246') and applies only after F4. The Linux build is already warning-free without it (0 warnings on every build). No value for Linux.

Drops EPICS 3.13 support: 27 files, about 1088 deletions (config/, Makefile.Vx/Host, 3.13 branches in AsynDriverInterface.cc, StreamEpics.cc, devStream.h), plus configure/RULES simplified to include $(CONFIG)/RULES. Dead-code removal with no change on Base 7.0.10. Fails alone on the pin only at the CHANGELOG hunk (context from removed doc commits); all code hunks apply. Builds with 0 warnings alone, with F8, F8+F9 and in the chain; full upstream suite on the chain matches baseline. Largest blast radius of the set for no functional gain, and it shifts StreamEpics.cc line offsets for F8 and F9.

Documentation, hyperlinks, PSI.png replaced by PSI.svg, configure/RELEASE example versions. Nothing the build uses (RELEASE.local overrides). On the pin 3 of 10 files have failing hunks: CHANGELOG.md, docs/index.html, docs/setup.html (2 of 4). Pure documentation churn.

Adds epicsAtExit hook that sets a static flag; protocolFinishHook then skips callbackRequest into the callback queue after epicsExit. Removes a possible exit-time use of stopped callback threads when a record is processed during shutdown. Small, local to StreamEpics.cc, no new dependency. Applies with offsets (only the CHANGELOG hunk rejects); builds clean alone and after F6, and with F6+F9. Flag is a plain int (no atomic), harmless in practice. I did not reproduce the exit-time fault, so the benefit rests on code reading.

Casts to unsigned char for ctype calls across 7 files (Binary, Checksum, Regexp, StreamEpics, StreamFormatConverter, StreamProtocol, Timestamp converters), and uint32_t d -> unsigned char d in hexsum and hexlrc. Verified the type narrowing is safe: hexlrc d+final_digit stays within 0xFF. Only matters for bytes with the high bit set, and glibc tolerates negative ctype arguments in -128..-1, so no visible effect on the target distributions. Applies clean on pin and baseline; with F6 present offsets differ; builds with 0 warnings alone and in the chain.

New behavior: %+x / %+X on input sign-extends when width digits are read or no width is given. It is a feature and opt-in, but it changes the meaning of '+' for any existing protocol that already writes %+x on input. Runtime (longin, fake TCP device): baseline 'FF'->255, 'FFFFFFFFFFFFFFFF'->-1; with F10 'FF'->-1, '80'->-128, '7F'->127, '0xFFFF'->-1, '%+2x' with 'F' (fewer digits than width) -> 15, plain %x unchanged at 255. Applies clean, 2 files, builds clean.

Casts dset function pointers to DEVSUPFUN in 21 device-support files. Base 7.0.10 devSup.h declares DEVSUPFUN as long (*)() in one branch. Evidence: built the baseline with make USR_CFLAGS=-std=gnu23 (gcc 14.2 emulating the gcc 15 default) and it fails with 'initialization of long int (*)(void) from incompatible pointer type' errors in devaoStream.c and others; the same flags on pin+baseline+F11 build with 0 errors. Hosts in the support matrix use gcc 14, so it is not needed today; it is insurance for a compiler bump. Purely mechanical, leaf files, applies clean.

Replaces eight-space recipe indent by a tab in three dependency rules in src/Makefile. The local StreamDevice-dbd-tab.p0.patch makes the same three changes (with an added comment), so on the baseline F12 is rejected '3 out of 3 hunks ignored'. Fully redundant for this environment; applies clean only on the bare pin.

One-token fix: sizeof(sco->val) (8-byte double) becomes sizeof(sco->sval) (40-byte string) in devscalcoutStream.c. Runtime evidence (scalcout record, fake TCP device sending 36 characters): baseline SVAL = "ABCDEFG" (7 chars), with fix SVAL = full 36-char string. scalcout is compiled into this build (calc present, recordtype in streamApp.dbd). Silent data truncation, no overflow. Applies clean on pin, baseline and the full chain.

defects.description: StreamFormatTypeStr[] in StreamProtocol.cc still has 7 entries (none..pseudo) but F4 adds enum needs_original_format (value 7). StreamProtocol.cc compileFormat debug2 prints StreamFormatTypeStr[streamFormat.type] and StreamCore.cc line 1343 error path indexes it: out-of-bounds pointer read (UB) when streamDebug>=2 and an input checksum is compiled. Not fatal in my run (testChecksumNR with streamDebug 2 passed) but latent.

Test added by F4 (regsub + crc8) cannot run in an environment built with PCRE= empty: regsub converter is not registered, protocol fails to compile ('No converter registered for format %/'). The fix is unreachable and untestable here.

Sign extension computes v |= -1L << n, a left shift of a negative value (undefined before C++20, defined by gcc in practice); and the width test end-input >= fmt.width counts a '0x' prefix as digits. Behavioral side effect: '+' on %x input changes meaning for any protocol already using it. Results matched intent in my runtime test.
Hunks patch lines introduced by F4 (debug messages), so F5 cannot be carried alone; its other two hunks are Windows or MinGW only.
The replacement streamApp DBD list drops asynRecord.dbd and the drvAsynIPServerPort registrar that the old asynRegistrars.dbd carried; streamApp only, not libstream.
CHANGELOG hunk (F6, F7 and F8) does not apply to the pin: context lines come from upstream commits not in the thirteen. Strip the CHANGELOG hunks when carrying; code hunks are unaffected.

scores.note: New checksum hv_mps (Spellman MPS) added to ChecksumConverter.cc only; feature, not a defect fix. Value only if Spellman MPS supplies are on the controls network. Verified at runtime: real streamApp + TCP peer, protocol out "%s%<hv_mps>" gave 123456789c (0x63, matches the source comment) and in-side check accepted it. Applies clean on pin and on pin+local patches; build 0 warnings; upstream testChecksum still passes.

Only streamApp/Makefile and deletion of asynRegistrars.dbd (demo app, not libstream/stream.dbd). Functionally replaces StreamDevice-no-vxi11.p0.patch: pin+F2 alone builds (make rc=0, whereas pin alone fails at link on undefined vxi11RegisterCommands). Does NOT apply on the baseline: patch reports 'Reversed (or previously applied)' because the local patch edits the file F2 deletes. Carrying it means dropping the local patch. Side effect: streamApp.dbd now loads whole asyn.dbd (adds asynInterposeDelay/Echo registrars and all asyn device supports); drops explicit asynRecord.dbd line. No new value over the existing local patch.
One-word typo in a debug() string in StreamCore.cc. Applies clean on pin and baseline, builds clean. No behavior change.

Checksum after regsub now checks the unmodified device input (new StreamFormatType needs_original_format, delta tracking in StreamCore::matchInput). Only matters when the regsub converter %# is used with a checksum. This environment builds with PCRE= empty: running upstream's new testChecksum on the F4 tree fails at protocol parse with 'No converter registered for format %/', so regsub does not exist in the shipped binary and the fix has no effect here (I could not run the new regsub test; host has only PCRE2, no pcre.h). Core-path change for every input checksum; regression check: pre-F4 testChecksum passes on the F4 tree. Defect: StreamFormatTypeStr[] (StreamProtocol.cc) was not extended for the new enum value 7, see defects. Applies with offset -11 (assumes F1 context) but cleanly without F1.

Replaces %zu/%zi with a Z macro in debug strings and a size_t loop var in a Windows-only function; MinGW-only effect. Edits lines that F4 introduces: alone it FAILS to apply on pin and on baseline (2 hunks rejected in ChecksumConverter.cc and StreamCore.cc); F4+F5 applies and builds clean. Zero compiler warnings were present in baseline build on gcc 14 anyway. Pure prerequisite chain on F4.

Drops EPICS 3.13 code: ~48 KB diff, deletes config/ dir, Makefile.Host/Vx, edits StreamEpics.cc, AsynDriverInterface.cc, devStream.h, devaoStream.c, devstringoutStream.c and changes configure/RULES to include $(CONFIG)/RULES. Applies and builds on baseline once the CHANGELOG.md hunk is removed (that hunk is rejected on pin: changelog is cumulative); F6+F8 builds. No benefit for 7.0.10 targets, large blast radius over core files and build rules; only reason to carry would be to make F7/F8 apply with smaller offsets.

Docs, links and a RELEASE default-path change plus binary docs/PSI.png deletion; no source change. Does not apply by itself on pin or baseline (docs/index.html, docs/setup.html hunks depend on F6 text); even after F6 plus the full upstream order, docs/setup.html hunk 3 still rejects (it depends on one of the six dropped doc commits). patch cannot do the PNG binary delta. configure/RELEASE is overridden by RELEASE.local in our recipe. No operational value.

Registers epicsAtExit hook that sets a static flag; protocolFinishHook then skips callbackRequest() during exit. Avoids queueing to a callback thread already being torn down in epicsExit, so cleaner IOC shutdown. Small (10 lines, StreamEpics.cc) but sits in core record-processing hook; flag is a plain non-atomic int. Without F6 the hunks apply with offsets +20/+68 (CHANGELOG hunk rejected); builds clean alone and with F6; S_base stack run of upstream tests exits cleanly. Could not provoke the shutdown race deterministically, so benefit is by code reading.

Casts to unsigned char for isspace/toupper/etc. in 7 files (Binary, Checksum, Regexp, StreamEpics, StreamFormatConverter, StreamProtocol, Timestamp) and uint32_t d -> unsigned char d in hexsum/hexlrc. Technically UB for negative char arguments with bytes >=0x80 from the device, but glibc ctype tables accept -128..255 so no observable fault on Debian/Rocky. Applies on baseline with offsets (up to +65), builds clean; the RegexpConverter.cc hunks cannot be compile-checked here (PCRE empty). Mechanical, low risk, low value.

Adds sign extension for %+x/%+X input in scanLong (StreamFormatConverter.cc, 12 lines) plus docs. Verified at runtime with real streamApp and longin records: pin+patches gives FFFE -> 65534, F10 gives -2; 7FFF -> 32767 in both; %+2x of 80 -> -128 on F10; width not fully used (%+4x of FE) stays 254; plain %4x unchanged. Feature, useful for signed 16-bit hex registers. Behavior change for any existing protocol that already writes %+x on input (previously flag ignored). Applies clean, builds clean.

Casts device-support table members to (DEVSUPFUN) in 21 dev*Stream.c files. No effect on gcc 14 (Debian 12/13, Rocky 8/10). I built baseline and F11 with USR_CFLAGS += -std=gnu23 (C23 semantics, as gcc 15 defaults): baseline fails with 'initialization of long (*)(void) from incompatible pointer type' in devaoStream.c and devStream.h, F11 builds (make rc=0). So it is future-proofing for gcc 15+/Debian 14/Fedora. Mechanical, applies on baseline with offset 2, no warnings.

Replaces eight-space indent with TAB on three dependency-rule recipe lines in src/Makefile. This is exactly what StreamDevice-dbd-tab.p0.patch already does (local patch also adds an explanatory comment). Applied on baseline: 'Reversed (or previously applied) patch detected', 3 of 3 hunks ignored. Applies clean on pristine pin. Fully redundant with the local patch; carrying adds nothing. Note on 7.0.10 the build already passes with the spaces (pin+F2 built OK).

One token: sizeof(sco->val) (8) -> sizeof(sco->sval) (40) as the bound of streamScanfN in devscalcoutStream.c readData. Verified at runtime with a real scalcout record plus TCP peer: reply 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123' lands in SVAL as 'ABCDEFG' (7 chars) on baseline and in full on F13. Affects scalcout records that use an in-string reply after an out (calc is built in this environment). Applies clean and builds clean; leaf file; truncation only, not a memory-safety bug.

defects.description: StreamFormatTypeStr[] in StreamProtocol.cc was not extended for the new enum value needs_original_format (7), but compileFormat debug2 and the 'not supported' error in StreamCore.cc index it by fmt.type. With streamDebug 2 on F4 every input checksum format logs 'format.type=' (empty) in StreamDebug.log: an out-of-bounds read of a char* table (observed benign here, undefined behavior). The range check 'type < 1 && type > pseudo_format' is pre-existing and never true, so needs_original_format is also not validated there.

Fix is dead in this deployment: with PCRE= empty the regsub converter is not built (log: 'No converter registered for format %/'), so upstream's added test cannot run in this build and the change only adds risk on the core input path for all checksum users.

Behavior change: protocols that already use %+x/%+X on input (flag previously ignored) now get sign extension when width digits are read or width is unset. Width test counts a 0x prefix toward the width, so a prefixed value shorter than the width in digits can be sign extended or not inconsistently. Minor.
Hunks of docs/setup.html do not apply even in complete upstream merge order from the pin (one rejected hunk), because the pin lacks a documentation-only upstream commit that was dropped from the set.

terminating is a plain static int written in an exit handler and read in record-processing threads without atomics; benign in practice at process exit, but records left with pact set are never completed once the flag is set.

scores.note: Adds hv_mps checksum (11 lines, one table row) in ChecksumConverter.cc. Ran %<hv_mps> on '123456789' through the real IOC and fake TCP peer: wire output 'c' (0x63), matches the upstream comment. New feature only valuable if a Spellman MPS supply is used; pure leaf, clean apply and build.

Replaces asynRegistrars.dbd with asyn.dbd+drvAsynIPPort+drvAsynSerialPort and drops vxi11. Pin raw build against asyn 4.46.0 fails (make rc=2) because vxi11 is gone; F2 alone builds (rc=0). Functionally supersedes local no-vxi11 patch, but fails to apply on baseline (deleted file content differs: 'Reversed or previously applied'). Resulting dbd gains asynInterposeDelay/Echo registrars, asynRecord and many asyn device supports. Redundant with baseline, so low urgency.
One-word typo in a debug() string. Applies and builds clean. No functional value.

Checksum after regsub uses original input. Needs RegexpConverter, which is not built in the ALS-U recipe (PCRE= empty): IOC log shows no regexp converter and protocol 'out %#/[0-9]{2}/&:/' fails with 'No converter registered for format %/'. So the fixed case cannot occur here. Patch alters StreamCore::matchInput for every input checksum (new needs_original_format type); existing testChecksum passes after it. Defect: StreamFormatTypeStr[] not extended (see defects). Prerequisite of F5.

Compiler-warning cleanup, mostly MinGW/Windows (_MINGW printf prefix, size_t loop var) plus %zu->Z macro in debug strings added by F4. Does not apply without F4 (2 hunks FAILED in ChecksumConverter.cc and StreamCore.cc). With F4 it builds clean; no Linux behaviour change.

Drops EPICS 3.13: deletes config/, Makefile.Host/Vx, docs page, and edits AsynDriverInterface.cc, StreamEpics.cc, devStream.h, configure/RULES (48 KB diff). Code part applies and builds on baseline and pin (CHANGELOG hunk fails, docs only). No benefit for a 7.0.10 build and the widest regression surface of the set; carrying it adds risk for nothing.

Docs, links, and configure/RELEASE version strings (overridden by RELEASE.local in the recipe). Code part applies; docs hunks fail on pin (CHANGELOG, index.html, setup.html). Binary PSI.png delete and svg swap. No runtime effect.

Registers epicsAtExit hook that sets 'terminating' and stops protocolFinishHook from queuing processCallback during epicsExit. Prevents callback work during shutdown. Applies with offsets and builds (CHANGELOG hunk only fails). Flag is a plain static int written at exit, read from other threads; benign. Not exercised at runtime by me.

Casts ctype arguments to unsigned char in 7 files (link-string parsing, scanLong, protocol parser, timestamp, checksum). Removes UB for bytes >=0x80; glibc tolerates negative values, so practical effect is low. Hunks apply with offsets; build clean; testInteger, testString, testFormats, testStrangesum, testRaw pass on the combined tree. Also changes hexsum/hexlrc temp from uint32_t to unsigned char.

New %+x signed-hex input. Ran real IOC with %+x and %+2x input: baseline gives FFFF=65535, 80=128; with F10 FFFF=-1, 80=-128, 7F=127. A feature, not a fix of existing behaviour; only matters for protocols that opt in with '+'. Leaf, applies and builds clean.

Casts dset function pointers to DEVSUPFUN in 21 dev*Stream.c. Built baseline with USR_CFLAGS=-std=gnu23 (gcc 14.2): fails with -Wincompatible-pointer-types errors in devaoStream.c; same build with F11 succeeds (rc=0). Matches gcc 15 default. Targets use gcc 14, so not urgent today, but needed on gcc 15. Mechanical, applies with offset 2, builds.

Replaces 8-space recipe indent with tabs in src/Makefile. Identical line changes to local StreamDevice-dbd-tab.p0.patch, so it is fully replaced; on baseline it fails to apply (reversed). Pin+no-vxi11 only builds on EPICS 7.0.10 anyway (rc=0), the tab issue matters on 7.0.11. Zero extra value over baseline.

sizeof(sco->val) -> sizeof(sco->sval). Verified with real IOC: scalcout reading 'ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789' stores 'ABCDEFG' on baseline, full 36 chars with F13. One-line, applies and builds on baseline; real data-loss bug for any stream scalcout with string input.

scores.note: New hv_mps checksum (additive table entry, hv_mps init 0xFF => 7-bit two's complement | 0x40). Ran real IOC with stringout %s%<hv_mps>: '' -> 0x40, 'A' -> 0x7F, 'AB' -> 0x7D, '123456789' -> 0x63; all match the formula and the upstream comment. Baseline reports 'Unknown checksum algorithm hv_mps'. Pure feature, useful only if ALS-U runs Spellman MPS supplies (not established); no behavior change for other protocols.

Replaces local no-vxi11 patch: deletes asynRegistrars.dbd and lists asyn.dbd/drvAsynIPPort.dbd/drvAsynSerialPort.dbd in streamApp/Makefile. Applies and builds on the bare pin (link succeeds); on baseline it conflicts with no-vxi11 (asynRegistrars.dbd hunk 'Reversed or previously applied'). Generated streamApp.dbd registrars equal baseline plus asynInterposeDelay/Echo (benign superset). Only the streamApp test IOC is affected, not libstream. Value is mostly to retire our own patch, not a new fix.
One debug() string typo ('unpared' -> 'unparsed'). No runtime effect. Applies and builds singly.

Adds needs_original_format enum and delta tracking in StreamCore::matchInput so checksum after regsub is computed over the unmodified input. In the ALS-U build PCRE= is empty so RegexpConverter is not compiled (nm shows no Regexp symbols; the F4 test line fails with 'No converter registered for format %/'): the fix has no runtime effect here. Regression surface is real though (every input checksum now takes the new branch): testChecksum with the regsub lines removed passes on base, F4 alone, F1, and all-fixes trees. Core file touch (StreamCore.cc, StreamFormat.h). Prerequisite of F5.

Fix warnings: Z printf prefix macro and MinGW/Windows loop type. Does not apply alone (ChecksumConverter hunk 2 and StreamCore hunk 1 reject on pin and baseline) because it edits debug lines introduced by F4. After F4 it applies and builds. Baseline gcc 14 -Wall build has zero warnings, so no benefit on Linux.

Drops EPICS 3.13 code: 27 files, ~1600-line diff, deletes config/, Makefile.Vx/Host, rewrites configure/RULES, class Stream/AsynDriverInterface inheritance. No functional change on Base 7.0.10; builds and test suite equals baseline, but large blast radius and overlaps StreamEpics.cc with F8/F9. Carrying it only adds risk (CHANGELOG hunk fails on pin; apply on top of baseline needs CHANGELOG excluded).

Documentation, PSI.svg/png swap, and configure/RELEASE version strings. patch cannot apply the PSI.png binary delete; docs/index.html and docs/setup.html hunks reject on the pin because they depend on doc commits that were dropped from the set. configure/RELEASE edit is overridden by RELEASE.local in our recipe. Zero code change; build identical.

epicsAtExit hook sets a static 'terminating' flag; protocolFinishHook skips queuing processCallback after exit began. Prevents callback work during epicsExit teardown (shutdown-time crash/hang class). Applies with offsets, builds, full test suite equals baseline. I could not reproduce the exit-time failure, so the benefit is from code reading. Flag is non-atomic int (benign at exit).

Casts char args of isspace/toupper/etc to unsigned char in 7 files (protocol parser, link string parser, converters). Fixes UB for bytes >127 on libc implementations that index tables; glibc tolerates negative indexes so no observable bug on our Debian/Rocky. hexsum/hexlrc d changed to unsigned char; testChecksum passes. Touches many files, applies with small offsets after F5/F6/F8.

New %+x/%+X signed hex input. Ran real IOC (longin, %+2x/%+3x/%+x): FF/2 -> -1, 80/2 -> -128, 7F/2 -> 127, FFFE (no width) -> -2, 0xFF -> -1, 8 -> -8; baseline gives 255/65534. Behavior change for any existing protocol that already uses %+x on input (previously unsigned). Edge defect: end-input counts the 0x prefix toward width, so '0xF' with %+3x gives -1 although only one digit was read (docs say only when width digits are read). -1L << n is formally UB. Feature rather than bug fix.

Casts dset function pointers to DEVSUPFUN in 21 dev*Stream.c. Verified: compiling all 21 files with gcc 14 -std=gnu2x -fsyntax-only (C23 empty-parens semantics, as in gcc 15) gives errors in 21/21 files on the pin and 0/21 with the fix. No effect on our current gcc 8/12/14. Pure compile-time, zero runtime change; protects the next distro move to gcc 15. Mechanical, clean apply, builds.

Tab indent in src/Makefile. Identical to the tab hunks already in local StreamDevice-dbd-tab.p0.patch: on baseline patch reports 'previously applied' for 3/3 hunks. Even without the tab fix, pin+no-vxi11 builds fine on Base 7.0.10 (make rc=0), so no effect on our recipe. Redundant duplicate of a local patch.

sizeof(sco->val) (8) -> sizeof(sco->sval) (40) in devscalcoutStream.c. Ran real IOC with a scalcout record reading '%s' of a 36-char line: baseline SVAL = 'ABCDEFG' (truncated at 8 incl. NUL); with fix SVAL = full 36 characters. Real functional bug (truncation, not overflow), one token, leaf file, applies clean and builds.

defects.description: The width test uses end-input (which includes a 0x prefix) so '0xF' read with %+3x is sign-extended to -1 although only one hex digit was read; docs say extension applies only when width digits are read. Observed on real IOC: DZ:hx3 '0xF' -> -1. Also left-shifts a negative long (formally UB), and changes existing behavior for protocols that already use %+x on input.

Fix has no effect without PCRE (RegexpConverter not built in our recipe). Code-read note, not run: needs_original_format bypasses the parse-time check 'Fieldname not allowed with pseudo format' in StreamProtocol.cc (only tests pseudo_format) and has no case in Stream::formatValue switch. Upstream docs sentence has a grammar slip ('if ignored').
No defect found. Upstream comment says the example checksum is 0x63; the shipped code reproduces it for '123456789' on a real IOC. No test was added upstream.
Not independently applicable: edits debug lines created by F4 (both ChecksumConverter and StreamCore hunks), so it must be carried together with F4.
Not appliable with patch as shipped: PSI.png binary deletion and docs hunks depend on documentation-only upstream commits that are not in the set.

Checksum after regsub must use original input. Needs PCRE for regsub (%#/../), but environment builds PCRE= empty: runtime converter list has no %/ or %#, and the new upstream testChecksum case fails at protocol parse here. So fix is inert for us. Touches matchInput core, adds enum value needs_original_format, changes parse return for every checksum when scanFormat. Drops EPICS 3.13 support: removes ~20 files and ifdefs in StreamEpics.cc, AsynDriverInterface.cc, configure/RULES now include $(CONFIG)/RULES. Builds clean on Base 7.0.10 but pure cleanup with large diff and no benefit to a 7.0.10 build; CHANGELOG hunk does not apply (needs excluding).

Registers epicsAtExit hook; sets terminating so protocolFinishHook stops scheduling processCallback during epicsExit, avoiding callback after teardown. Builds and tests pass; src hunks apply, only CHANGELOG hunk fails. Benefit is at IOC shutdown only. Touches protocolFinishHook, a core path, though change is one condition.

Casts ctype arguments to unsigned char in 7 files; fixes UB for negative char (non-ASCII input) and hexsum/hexlrc local type. glibc tolerates -128..255 so practical effect small; applies on pin and baseline, builds clean, mechanical.

New %+x signed hex input. My testF10 (longin, %+2x FF -> -1, 80 -> -128, %+x FFFF -> -1, 0x8000 -> -32768, %x FF -> 255 unchanged) passes on chain and fails on baseline (65535, 32768). Feature rather than bug fix, opt-in via flag so low regression surface. Code reading: sign test input[i]>'7' also accepts non-hex letters but strtoul has already bounded the digits.

Casts dset function pointers to DEVSUPFUN in 21 dev*Stream.c. Verified: baseline with USR_CFLAGS=-std=gnu2x (gcc 15 default) fails with incompatible-pointer-types errors; with F11 builds rc=0. Default gcc 14 builds on both, so no harm today on Debian 12/13 and Rocky 8/10; protects future gcc 15 platforms. Mechanical and locality good though many files.

Replaces 8-space recipe lines in src/Makefile by tabs. Local dbd-tab patch already does the same: on baseline git apply fails (already applied), on pin alone it applies. Pin without our patches fails to link only because of vxi11 (not Makefile). No added value over local patch; only allows retiring it.

One-token fix, applies clean on pin and baseline, builds clean. Environment builds scalcout (CALC set), so affected. Runtime demo not achieved: record post-processing overwrote SVAL in my attempt, so evidence is code and header reading. Commit date in patch header is 2026-08-10.
